h: 5.2.1 Write path: batches, outbound tick, hot WAL in Redis (ADR-028)
t: A room applies updates as they arrive and queues them. At most every 40 ms (armed by the first queued item) it appends the queue as one batch, then sends one merged update frame and one presence frame shared by every peer. Nothing is fanned out before the batch is durable; a failed append closes the room with 1012 and fans nothing out. Without Redis the WAL is room_updates in the database (one guarded multi-row insert per batch; on SQLite one writer task commits many rooms' batches per transaction). With Redis ( OC_WAL_REDIS_URL , default REDIS_URL ) the hot WAL is one stream per room, oc:wal:

Yrs apply + broadcast ≈ 10–50 µs per small update; 300 rooms × 10 upd/s = 3 000 upd/s ≪ capacity. Bottleneck is fan-out bytes, not merge. Memory: ~ 3× doc size per live room; 300 rooms × 1 MB × 3 ≈ 900 MB worst, typical 100–200 MB.

Per-host keys; JWT aud , iss , exp ≤ 10 h , jti replay cache. Role enforced server-side per frame ; client UI is advisory only. h: We already use Collabora through WOPI. Can we reuse that?
t: Yes. OpenCanvas is a WOPI client: discovery, CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile and PUT_RELATIVE, with an allow-list for the WOPISrc URLs it will call. Proof keys are not supported yet. See WOPI mode .

h: What can it import and export?
t: Export: Markdown, HTML, JSON, the native .ocanvas file, Word, and PDF when the operator runs the optional Gotenberg sidecar (otherwise the editor prints to PDF). Whiteboards export as SVG and PNG. Import: Markdown, HTML and CSV. See Operations .

One node runs on SQLite. For more users, run several nodes against MySQL or MariaDB with Redis: each room has one owner node, other nodes relay to it, and if the owner dies another node takes the room over from its log. See Operations and Architecture .

h: Does the demo send anything anywhere?
t: No. The demo is the real editor running against a document in your browser, with simulated collaborators. There is no server behind it, and exports that need a server say so. Its assistant plays a scripted run: no model is called.

h: Where does the assistant send my content?
t: Only to the model server the operator configures: the Claude Platform, or a self-hosted model through vLLM, Ollama or llama.cpp. The OpenCanvas server makes that call, never the browser, and it keeps no prompts or answers. AI is off unless the operator turns it on for your app. A self-hosted model needs tool calling for the assistant to edit; without it, it can only answer. See AI and MCP .

The server, the editor and the sample host on your machine, from the project's README. To look around first, open the demo : it runs in your browser with no server. Alpha: v0.1.0-alpha.1. For evaluation, with no production SLA. Read the release notes and its known limitations (memory, durability modes, WOPI without proof keys, single node first) before you deploy it. The AI assistant and MCP endpoint are experimental and off by default .

Product: OpenCanvas — an embeddable, real-time collaborative canvas (rich document + board) built for integration . Status: draft v0.1, 2026-11-21. Awaiting approval. Owner: schnsrw1@gmail.com

Every product that wants a "Slack/Zoom/Loop-style canvas" today has two bad options: build a collaborative editor from scratch (months of CRDT, cursor, conflict and export work) or adopt a SaaS whose storage, users and permissions are not theirs. Collabora Online solved this for office files: the host keeps files, users and ACLs, the editor does editing. Nobody offers that model for a modern block canvas.

Drop one iframe (or one web component) into any app and its users get a live, multi-cursor canvas — text, tables, images, links, embeds and boards — while the app keeps full ownership of the file, the users and who can do what.

Host owns identity, ACL and storage. OpenCanvas never authenticates users, never decides permissions, never keeps the canonical file. We own editing. Real-time merge, presence, cursors, preview, export, commit back to host. No document persistence beyond a live session. Session state (CRDT snapshot + update tail) is kept only to survive node restarts and to let late joiners catch up; it is deleted after commit + idle TTL. Lightweight. One server binary; SQLite by default; one JS bundle. Runs on a 1 vCPU / 512 MB box for a small team. Scalable. Stateless HTTP, room-affine WebSocket nodes, MySQL

Where OpenCanvas stands and what comes next, generated from the project's roadmap and its execution tracker. Every unit of work has a row there; this page shows each row's status as the tracker records it. This is the project's plan, not a commitment. No dates are promised. "Built, in review" means the work is merged and verified and waits for the owner's approval. Ideas and requests are welcome as GitHub issues .

OpenCanvas integrates with any third-party application through standardized APIs and SDKs, without depending on specific CasualOffice products. Hosts connect through the documented launch tokens, callbacks, WOPI, REST, postMessage, the <open-canvas> SDK and MCP; nothing in the server or editor assumes a particular host. This keeps the project independent and modular, and open to a broad developer ecosystem (ADR-038).
